title: Circles: Chords and Angles
seo_title: Circles Class 9 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre and conversely; the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord and conversely; equal chords are equidistant from the centre and conversely; the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle at any point on the remaining part of the circle; angles in the same segment are equal; the sum of either pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180° and its converse (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Circles worksheet (NCERT Chapter 9): chords and distances from the centre, equal chords, angle at the centre, angles in the same segment and cyclic quadrilaterals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference
key_sub: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add up to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

Chords: the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, so half chord² + distance² = radius². Equal chords are equidistant from the centre and subtend equal angles at the centre.

Angles: the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the rest of the circle. Angles in the same segment are equal; the angle in a semicircle is 90°.

In a cyclic quadrilateral each pair of opposite angles adds up to 180°.

Example

A chord is 8 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. Find its length.

Half chord = √(10² − 8²) = 6

Answer: 12 cm

Example

ABCD is cyclic and ∠A = 75°. Find ∠C.

Opposite angles add up to 180°

Answer: 105°

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to double the half chord found by Pythagoras.
  • Making the angle at the circumference double the angle at the centre. It is half.
  • Taking the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral as equal. They add up to 180°.

faq.q: What is the perpendicular bisector property of a chord?
faq.a: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, and the line from the centre to the mid-point of a chord is perpendicular to it.

faq.q: What is the relation between the angle at the centre and at the circumference?
faq.a: The angle at the centre is double the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
A quadrilateral whose vertices all lie on a circle. Its opposite angles add up to 180°.

faq.q: How many circles pass through three non-collinear points?

sets.title: Chords and the perpendicular from the centre

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. OM is perpendicular to the chord AB, OM = 40 cm and the radius is 58 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.e: OM bisects AB. MB = √(58² − 40²) = √1764 = 42 cm, so AB = 2 × 42 = 84 cm.

items.q: The line drawn through the centre of a circle to bisect a chord is ___ to the chord.
items.e: perpendicular.

items.q: A quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on a circle is called ___.

items.q: AB and CD are chords of a circle with centre O and radius 40 cm. AB = CD = 64 cm. How far is CD from O?
items.e: Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Distance = √(40² − 32²) = 24 cm.

items.q: In a circle with centre O, chord AB = 44 cm and chord CD = 48 cm. Which chord is closer to O?
c: They are the same distance from O
You cannot tell without the radius
items.e: The longer chord is closer to the centre (the half-chord is longer, so the distance √(r² − half²) is smaller): CD.

items.q: Complete the statement: Two equal chords in the same circle …
c: are the same distance from the centre
items.e: This is a symmetry property of circles: two equal chords in the same circle are the same distance from the centre.

items.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm, chords PQ and RS are both 8 cm from the centre. PQ = 12 cm. What is RS?

sets.title: Angles in the same segment and in a semicircle

items.q: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. ∠ACB = 26°. What is ∠ADB + ∠ACB?
items.e: Angles in the same segment are equal, so ∠ADB = 26° and the sum is 52°.

items.q: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. ∠CAB = 67°. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so ∠ACB = 90°. ∠ABC = 180° − 90° − 67° = 23°.

items.q: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. ∠CAB = 27°. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so ∠ACB = 90°. ∠ABC = 180° − 90° − 27° = 63°.

items.q: AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. ∠CAB = 33°. Find ∠OCB.
items.e: OB = OC (radii), so ∠OCB = ∠OBC. ∠ACB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠ABC = 90° − 33° = 57°. ∠OCB = 57°.

items.q: A, B, C and D lie on a circle, and the chords AC and BD cross. ∠BAC = 38°. Find ∠BDC.
items.e: ∠BAC and ∠BDC both stand on arc BC, so they are equal: 38°.

items.q: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. ∠ACB = 65°. Find ∠ADB.
items.e: ∠ACB and ∠ADB stand on the same arc AB (angles in the same segment), so ∠ADB = 65°.

items.q: A, B, C and D lie on a circle. ∠ACB = 40°. What is ∠ADB + ∠ACB?

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. ∠AOB = 142°. Find ∠OAB.
items.e: OA = OB (radii), so △OAB is isosceles: ∠OAB = (180° − 142°) ÷ 2 = 19°.

items.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. ∠DAB = 80°. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180° (angles in opposite segments): ∠BCD = 180° − 80° = 100°.

items.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and DC is extended to E. ∠DAB = 96°. Find ∠BCE.
items.e: ∠BCD = 180° − 96° = 84°, so ∠BCE = 180° − 84° = 96°. The exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.
